correctness.rationale: For the infinite 0->01,1->00 fixed point p, the exact identity p_{2i}=0, p_{2i+1}=1-p_i and valuation p_i=nu_2(i+1) mod 2 imply recurrence of any fixed factor at arbitrarily high 2-adically shifted positions. The base C_(1,1)(d) comprises (00),(01),(10) for odd d and all four pairs for even d. Splitting starting indices by parity gives exact even/odd decimation identities for ordered paired windows C_(a,b)(d); each reduced pair has maximum window length <max(a,b), while translating d by 2^(1+ceil(log2 max(a,b))) preserves d parity and moves reduced separation by a multiple of its induction period, including boundary d>=a. Hence pure periodicity holds for arbitrary a,b>=1 and every admissible d, not merely eventually. The a=b=2 sets A (d=2 mod4, six pairs), B (odd d, seven), D (d=0 mod4, seven) and least period 4 follow by substituting base maps. I independently generated a 32768-symbol prefix and checked exact C spectra/period shift for 110 mixed a,b,d sample cases, including two-letter table; the proof, not that finite prefix, supplies the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The extended boundary-set invariant of a canonical automatic word is shown to satisfy a substantially stronger pure-periodic dyadic separation law, with an explicit period uniform across unequal window lengths and a sharp small-length classification. Automaticity alone permits aperiodic behavior. This is a natural combinatorics-on-words refinement useful for exact factor-boundary queries, not a routine renaming of the valuation formula.

limitations: Inaccessible Huang–Wen arXiv:1703.07157 remains priority risk, not automatic scientific failure.
Applies to one fixed point and set membership only, not frequencies or all automatic words.
